classification.difficultyReason: Fix one edge, identify the remaining edges sharing either endpoint without counting crossings as vertices, and compare this count with all remaining edges.

content.prompt: In the figure below, each of the five vertices is connected to the other four vertices by one edge. Two of the edges are randomly chosen. Find the probability that the edges both connect to the same vertex.

spec.description: Five black marked vertices in a pentagonal arrangement, with all ten straight edges. Crossings remain unmarked. Coordinates reproduce topology and approximate proportions; no dimensions are asserted.
spec.mathematics: Complete graph on five vertices. Each vertex has four incident edges.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied graph is visible in the question; no answer annotations are included.

inlines.text: After choosing one edge, six of the nine remaining edges share one of its endpoints.

answer.worked:
There are ten edges. After one edge is chosen, nine remain. At each endpoint of the chosen edge, three other edges meet it. These six edges are distinct; unmarked crossings are not vertices.

$$\begin{align*}\Pr(\text{shared vertex})&=\frac{3+3}{9}\\\Pr(\text{shared vertex})&=\frac{6}{9}\\\Pr(\text{shared vertex})&=\frac{2}{3}.\end{align*}$$
